# Sources — `counsel:residential-real-estate-closings`

Check these before answering on anything they cover, and cite what you used. The use note on each one is binding: most of what a professional cites is free to read and not free to reproduce.

## 12 CFR § 1024.14 — Prohibition against kickbacks and unearned fees (RESPA Section 8)

Consumer Financial Protection Bureau · US · public domain (US government) — quote freely

<https://www.consumerfinance.gov/rules-policy/regulations/1024/14/>

**Authoritative for:** Why no fee or thing of value may pass for the referral of settlement-service business, including between an attorney's own businesses, and what an affiliated-business arrangement must disclose.

## 12 CFR § 1026.19 — Certain mortgage and variable-rate transactions (TILA-RESPA integrated disclosures)

Consumer Financial Protection Bureau · US · public domain (US government) — quote freely

<https://www.consumerfinance.gov/rules-policy/regulations/1026/19/>

**Authoritative for:** The Loan Estimate within three business days of application and the Closing Disclosure received three business days before consummation, with the changes that restart the waiting period — the lender's clock that a closing date is built around.

## Amendments to the Graduated Percent Fee on realty transfers over $1 million

New Jersey Division of Taxation · NJ · **read and cite only — copyrighted, do not reproduce**

<https://www.nj.gov/treasury/taxation/pdf/lpt/GraduatedPercentFeeNotice.pdf>

**Authoritative for:** The Division's notice implementing P.L. 2025, c. 69: for deeds on or after July 10, 2025 the former 1% buyer-paid fee is a seller-paid fee of 1% to 3.5% of the entire consideration, with the refund procedure for contracts signed before the effective date.

## N.J.A.C. 11:5-6.2 — Contracts of sale, leases and listing agreements (the attorney review clause)

New Jersey Real Estate Commission (text as republished by the Legal Information Institute) · NJ · public domain — quote freely

<https://www.law.cornell.edu/regulations/new-jersey/N-J-A-C-11-5-6-2>

**Authoritative for:** The attorney review clause a real estate licensee must include in a contract for a one-to-four-family home or a vacant one-family lot: three business days from delivery, counted excluding Saturdays, Sundays and legal holidays, during which either party's attorney may disapprove the contract. The Commission's own site links to a commercial republication of Title 11:5; this is the readable copy of the same text.

## New Jersey Division of Taxation — Bulk Sales

New Jersey Division of Taxation · NJ · **read and cite only — copyrighted, do not reproduce**

<https://www.nj.gov/treasury/taxation/bulk_sale_act.shtml>

**Authoritative for:** The bulk sale notification (Form C-9600) a purchaser files at least ten days before closing under N.J.S.A. 54:50-38, and the Division's reading of the simple-dwelling-house exemption for sales by an individual, estate or trust.

## New Jersey Division of Taxation — Nonresident sellers of real property

New Jersey Division of Taxation · NJ · **read and cite only — copyrighted, do not reproduce**

<https://www.nj.gov/treasury/taxation/individuals/nonsellers-property.shtml>

## New Jersey Division of Taxation — Realty Transfer Fee

New Jersey Division of Taxation · NJ · **read and cite only — copyrighted, do not reproduce**

<https://www.nj.gov/treasury/taxation/realty.shtml>

**Authoritative for:** The current realty transfer fee schedules, the partial exemptions for senior citizens, blind or disabled persons and low-and-moderate-income housing, and the Graduated Percent Fee on transfers over $1,000,000 with the affidavit forms each requires.

## New Jersey Rules of Court, including the Rules of Professional Conduct

New Jersey Judiciary · NJ · public domain — quote freely

<https://www.njcourts.gov/attorneys/rules-of-court>

**Authoritative for:** The court rules that set the practice's clocks and duties — R. 1:3-1 (computing time), R. 1:21-6 (attorney trust and business accounts and their records), R. 1:21-7 (contingent fees), R. 4:80-6 (notice of probate and proof of mailing), R. 4:85-1 and 4:85-2 (the will-contest window) — and the Rules of Professional Conduct, which are an appendix to Part I: RPC 1.2, 1.4, 1.5, 1.6, 1.7, 1.8, 1.14, 1.15, 5.1, 5.3, 5.4, 7.1 through 7.4. Amended annually by the Supreme Court's omnibus order, ordinarily effective September 1.

## New Jersey Statutes — current text

New Jersey Legislature, Office of Legislative Services · NJ · public domain — quote freely

<https://lis.njleg.state.nj.us/nxt/gateway.dll?f=templates&fn=default.htm>

Machine-readable: <https://pub.njleg.state.nj.us/statutes/>

**Authoritative for:** The current text of every New Jersey statute cited here — Title 3B (wills, probate, intestacy, fiduciary commissions, refunding bonds, the Uniform Trust Code), Title 46 (powers of attorney, the realty transfer fee and the Graduated Percent Fee), Title 26 (advance directives), Title 54 (the transfer inheritance tax and the bulk sale notice) and Title 52 (remote notarial acts). Read the section; a summary on a firm's website is not the law.
